issues.description: Constructor parameter order mismatch for class Meal: the problem statement (UML) and the solution repository define the constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template repository defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). The template's constructor order contradicts the UML and solution and also conflicts with the example usage in Main (new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})). This will cause compilation errors or confusion for students following the examples or UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template repository Meal constructor to match the UML and solution: change the signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and reorder the constructor body accordingly (assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;). Also ensure example usages in Main (if uncommented) remain in the name-then-ingredients order.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for the Meal concept is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement (UML) and the solution repository define the Meal constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, ingredients second). The template repository implements the constructor as public Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first, name second). Additionally, the example usage in the template's Main.java instantiates Meal with the name as the first argument (new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})), which expects the name-first constructor. This mismatch (parameter order reversed) prevents a clear mapping from the specification to the template implementation and can lead to compilation errors or confusion when students try to follow the examples or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the specification and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;. Ensure any example usages (e.g., Main.java) and tests align with this parameter order.
